issue.title: Question about the choice of input data (log-normalized) for the diffusion model
issue.body:
Dear Author,

Hello! I have read your paper with great interest. As a newcomer to this field, I have a few questions regarding some details that were not mentioned in this video (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tmyuSya_hUM&t=931s):

① After preprocessing gene and cell filtering, it seems you used log-normalized data (all positive values) as input. I have reviewed some related literature, such as scFoundation and STATE, which use raw counts as input, while other models use scaled data (resulting in both positive and negative values). Could you share the reasoning behind your choice of input data?

② Diffusion models are indeed a milestone in generative models, but DDPM was originally designed for images (grayscale or RGB, where values are typically constrained to [-1,1] or [0,1]). Do biological expression data require additional normalization or scaling before being fed into the model?

③ Since log-normalized data is used as input, you mentioned in the method section that the semantic encoder uses ReLU, while the diffusion model uses SiLU. To my knowledge, SiLU does not guarantee non-negative outputs like ReLU does. When I trained the diffusion model with the same input for 200 epochs, the predicted results from the saved .pt file contained negative values and were unrealistically scaled. Could you provide some insights into this?

I would greatly appreciate your response. Thank you for your time and contribution to the field!

comments.body:
Once again, I truly appreciate your work in advancing the field of virtual cells. I have been learning about diffusion models and wrote a conditional diffusion model code myself. However, since diffusion models only predict the noise added at each step, in practice I am unable to ensure that the final generated expression profiles follow a distribution at the same scale. For example, when I input log-normalized expression profiles (with all expression values greater than 0), the model outputs expression profiles distributed across a very wide range, including negative values. Therefore, I would still like to ask you about normalization-related issues.

Looking forward to your reply. I’m not sure when you will see this message, but I wish you a Happy Chinese New Year in advance!

Dear Zijiang, 

I am very sorry for my late response due to my super crazy schedule these two months. Thank you very much for your kind words and for taking the time to carefully read our paper and watch the talk. These are excellent questions, and here are my own opinions:

1. choice of log-normalized expression as input: You are absolutely right that there is no single "standard" choice here, and different generative models make different trade-offs. In Squidiff, we chose log-normalized expression primarily for numerical stability. The log-normalization will reduce the dynamic range and decrease the sparsity of the data, which helps stabilize diffusion training rather than discrete counts. However, there might be batch effect issues for Squidiff when training large scale of the datasets across different experiments. Thus a preprocessing and normalization of the whole training datsets would be required. Also since Squidiff is not a foundation model, we didn't consider the batch effect here. Actually, raw-count could work too in diffusion model too as long as the output being processed during the optimization. 

2. normalization of biological data for diffusion models: you are correct that diffusion model were orignally developed for images with bounded ranges. In scRNA data, we do not require strict normalization to [-1, 1], but log-normalization can restrict large dispersion of gene expression to a smaller range. Also, the diffusion model is learning to predict noise rather than raw expression values, there is no strict requirement that the data be range-bounded. 

3. The diffusion model itself is not constrained to produce non-negative outputs at every denoising step, especially we use SiLU to learn the noise which is actually have negative values. 

4. For your experience with model outputs expression profiles distributed across a very wide range, I have met with similar issues too in some of the cases. I feel it usually indicate a failure of training due to multiple reasons, maybe could you provide more details of your issue? 


Also could you send me email if you have further questions but I didn't answer timely? I check github less frequently than email. Thanks!
